assumptions: Assay interference by formulation buffers or capture reagents can be identified and controlled with spike-in and buffer-compatibility controls.
BODIPY C11 and orthogonal chemistries (TBARS, targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS) have sufficient sensitivity on low-biomass capture-positive fractions after method optimization.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program-level observations indicate EV-associated measures are sensitive to handling and downstream processing; lipid peroxidation and increased membrane permeability are mechanistically upstream events that would abolish membrane-protection of luminal cargo and surface-phenotype readouts, explaining loss of capture-protection co-localization despite preserved particle counts. One plausible route to such damage is repeated freeze-thaw applied in the presence of low concentrations of non-ionic surfactant and device-shear, which can together promote oxidative and physicochemical membrane compromise.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative per-lot pass/fail based on observed increase in peroxidation/permeability in capture-positive fractions after defined downstream exposures (no numeric limits).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV membrane chemical integrity and permeability
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Direct chemical readouts (lipid peroxidation, membrane permeability) report membrane integrity upstream of capture/protection loss and can serve as early stability/process damage indicators.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: assays require adaptation for low-biomass capture fractions and linkage to orthogonal capture/protection readouts must be empirically validated.

edges.competing_explanation: Epitope masking or selective loss of minor EV subpopulations (not chemical membrane damage) could reduce capture signal without clear peroxidation signatures.
edges.missing_experiment: Direct measurement of lipid-oxidation and permeability on capture-positive fractions after matrixed downstream exposures.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal membrane-protection assays and notes processing sensitivity; program rodent data highlight processing-dependence but do not measure lipid peroxidation directly.

edges.competing_explanation: Loss of in vivo detectability may be dominated by administration or species clearance rather than manufacturing-induced identity loss.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recoverability using materials passing vs failing the chemistry/protection gate.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal intranasal detectability concerns increase operational risk if identity is lost, but cross-species delivery barriers may confound interpretation.

nodes.statement: Downstream exposure combination (freeze-thaw during fill/finish + short contact with low-level non-ionic surfactant + device-shear rinse) increases EV membrane lipid peroxidation and membrane permeability.

Increased lipid peroxidation and membrane permeability cause loss of membrane-protection of luminal cargo and reduction or loss of multi-epitope intact surface-phenotype capture that normally co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive.

Loss of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-protection co-localization) despite similar NTA/TRPS particle counts will render lots analytically indistinguishable from secretome for identity and potency gating, blocking downstream bridging decisions.

competing_explanations: Epitope masking or selective loss of minor EV subpopulations rather than bulk membrane chemical damage.
Delivery or species-specific clearance dominates in vivo detectability issues independent of manufacturing-induced membrane damage.
dependencies: Analytical method development for low-biomass peroxidation and permeability assays
Validated spike-in tracer and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Availability of >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank/passage range
design_question: Daily question: Does the specific downstream exposure combination — controlled freeze-thaw cycles applied during fill/finish followed by short contact with a low-concentration non-ionic surfactant (representative nasal excipient) and device-shear rinse — reproducibly induce EV membrane lipid-peroxidation and membrane permeability that precedes and predicts loss of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) while leaving bulk particle counts nominally unchanged?
expected_measurable_effect: Exposed samples will show increased lipid-peroxidation readout (BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio and orthogonal TBARS or oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS), increased membrane-permeability dye uptake in capture-positive eluates, and concurrent loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and loss of detergent/protease-sensitive behavior, while bulk NTA/TRPS particle counts remain similar.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal panel per sample/fraction: (1) particle counts (NTA/TRPS) per density/size fraction; (2) intact immuno-capture for canonical surface markers with spike-in tracer readout and detergent+protease protection test; (3) BODIPY C11 ratiometric fluorescence on captured eluates (peroxidation); (4) membrane-permeability dye uptake on captured eluates; (5) TBARS and targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS (where material allows) as orthogonal chemistry confirmation; (6) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched within-lot arms: baseline handling (no freeze-thaw, no surfactant, no device shear) versus matrixed exposures combining 0/1/3 freeze-thaw cycles applied during simulated fill/finish crossed with short contact (predefined time) with low-level non-ionic surfactant buffer and low/medium device-shear rinse. All samples receive identical spike-in prior to exposure.
experiment.control: Positive controls: detergent-disrupted captured eluates and intentionally oxidized EV preparations (if available) to confirm BODIPY C11 and TBARS response. Spike-in tracer recovery required for per-sample assay validation. Capture-compatibility buffer-only controls to exclude reagent interference.
dependencies: Method development to adapt BODIPY C11 and permeability assays to low-biomass capture eluates
Capture-compatibility panels established before interpreting loss of capture signal
Sufficient conditioned-medium yields to run matrixed downstream exposures across >=3 lots
experiment.failure_criterion: Validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls confirm assay performance but (A) no reproducible peroxidation/permeability signal differences are observed across the downstream exposure matrix, or (B) peroxidation/permeability signals do not correlate with loss of capture-protection co-localization across >=3 lots; in either case the hypothesis is falsified.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, do not adopt lipid-oxidation/permeability as a manufacturing exclusion gate for the tested downstream exposures; re-evaluate other process stages (TFF envelope, pre-SEC strategies, source-cell variables) as primary drivers of intact-EV signature loss.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Controlled downstream exposures (freeze-thaw during fill/finish + short exposure to low-concentration non-ionic surfactant + device-shear rinse) cause measurable increases in membrane lipid peroxidation and permeability in capture-positive particle fractions and this chemical damage precedes and predicts loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative increase in BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio (and orthogonal TBARS/oxidized-phospholipid evidence when available) AND positive membrane-permeability dye uptake in capture-positive particle-peak fractions after the defined downstream exposure combination, concurrent with loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and loss of detergent/protease-sensitive behavior; NTA/TRPS particle counts remain nominally similar.
experiment.question: Does combined freeze-thaw during fill/finish plus short contact with a low-concentration non-ionic surfactant and a device-shear rinse reproducibly induce EV membrane lipid-peroxidation and permeability that predict loss of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature while particle counts remain similar?
required_material: >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same MSC source-cell bank (matched passage) processed to produce a bounded small-EV fraction (program-defined) sufficient for matrixing
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) for per-sample recovery controls
Candidate nasal excipient: representative low-concentration non-ionic surfactant formulation buffer (operator-selected surfactant class and concentration matrix)
Device-shear simulation rig or representative nasal delivery device for shear exposure
Controlled freeze-thaw capability to apply defined cycles during a simulated fill/finish step (0,1,3 cycles)
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
BODIPY C11 reagent and fluorescence reader configured for low-biomass fractions; TBARS reagents as orthogonal peroxidation check; targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS capability if material allows
Membrane-permeability dye reagents adapted for captured eluates (e.g., dye uptake assay), protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents, and detergent (Triton X-100) for protection assays
Density-fractionation materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (assay validation)
Correlation matrix: per-sample lipid-oxidation/permeability change versus capture-protection co-localization signal loss
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, at least one defined downstream-exposure combination (for example: 3 controlled freeze-thaw cycles during simulated fill/finish + short contact with low-level non-ionic surfactant + medium device-shear rinse) reproducibly produces (A) increased BODIPY C11 oxidation ratio and orthogonal peroxidation evidence in capture-positive particle-peak fractions, (B) positive membrane-permeability dye uptake in captured eluates, and (C) concurrent loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and loss of detergent/protease-sensitive behavior, while bulk particle counts remain similar and spike-in recovery confirms assay performance. If observed, the exposure envelope is designated an identity-loss gate.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Chemical membrane damage (lipid peroxidation/permeability) is an upstream mechanistic cause of loss of capture-protection co-localization.
Inference: Preserving lipid chemical integrity during fill/finish and formulation/device exposure will preserve orthogonal intact-EV signatures even if particle counts are similar.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls confirm assay performance, but the downstream exposure matrix (freeze-thaw applied during fill/finish + low-level non-ionic surfactant contact + device-shear rinse) does not reproducibly increase lipid peroxidation or membrane permeability in capture-positive fractions across >=3 independent lots, nor does it reproducibly abolish the capture-protection co-localization signature — hypothesis falsified.

If chemistry readouts change but capture-protection co-localization remains intact (decoupled), the proposed causal chain (peroxidation -> loss of capture/protection) is not supported and hypothesis is falsified.
human_decisions_required: Select representative non-ionic surfactant(s) and concentrations for the matrix (operator must choose specific excipient examples).
Define the freeze-thaw profile to be applied during simulated fill/finish (number and temperature range).
Select device-shear simulation parameters reflective of intended clinical device(s).
manufacturability_assessment: The proposed downstream-exposure gate targets common fill/finish and formulation/device conditions; identifying prohibited envelopes is implementable in process control documents. Chemistry- and protection-based assays will require method development and limited material but are compatible with pilot GMP runs as qualitative gates (non-numeric).
manufacturing_rationale: Fill/finish and device compatibility steps are operationally likely to include freeze-thaw exposures, transient surfactant contact (stabilizers/diluents), and device-associated shear. Identifying a prohibited envelope will allow upstream process design or formulation choices that preserve an orthogonal intact-EV signature and avoid wasted bridging work from process-damaged lots.
measurement_strategy: Matrixed, within-lot paired exposures with per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in controls and capture-compatibility panels. Primary analytics: particle counts (NTA/TRPS), intact immuno-capture co-localization assay (multi-epitope), detergent+protease protection, BODIPY C11 ratiometric peroxidation, TBARS orthogonal check, membrane-permeability dye uptake on captured eluates, and targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS when material allows. No numeric acceptance limits; qualitative pass/fail per lot/condition.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis is novel because it specifies a discrete, operational downstream-exposure envelope (freeze-thaw applied during fill/finish combined with short contact with a low-level non-ionic surfactant and device-shear rinse) and proposes chemistry-centered, membrane-focused readouts (BODIPY C11 peroxidation + membrane-permeability dye on capture-positive fractions) as early, qualitative stability/process-damage indicators that are causally linked to loss of orthogonal capture-protection identity metrics. Prior program hypotheses have considered freeze-thaw and formulation effects and TFF-envelope sensitivity, but none have (A) combined the specific fill/finish freeze-thaw timing with surfactant + device-shear as a single discriminating exposure, nor (B) proposed direct chemistry-based lipid-peroxidation and permeability assays on capture-positive fractions as the primary early discriminators.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity: lipid-chemistry and permeability assays may lack sensitivity on low-biomass capture fractions without optimization.
Assay interference: formulation/excipient components may interfere with peroxidation/permeability chemistries or capture reagents and require compatibility controls.
Scope: Even if manufacturing-induced damage is identified, in vivo cross-species delivery barriers may still prevent translational success.
proposed_potency_relationship: If lipid-oxidation/permeability and loss of capture-protection co-localization occur, protected-cargo-dependent in vitro anti-inflammatory activity (if present) is expected to be abolished; thus chemistry/protection attributes act as upstream indicators that predict loss of membrane-protected potency.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, declare the identified downstream-exposure envelope (defined freeze-thaw exposure combined with low-level non-ionic surfactant contact and device-shear rinse) as a prohibited downstream-process condition (identity-loss gate) and adopt chemistry- and protection-based stability readouts (membrane-peroxidation + permeability + loss of capture-protection co-localization) as qualitative, non-numeric process acceptance attributes for SGL-001.
title: Hypothesis: Combined freeze-thaw during fill/finish plus low-level non-ionic surfactant exposure causes EV membrane lipid-peroxidation and loss of orthogonal intact-EV signature
